mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar FEDFUNDS up moves, or the change is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 50,000 jobs predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are negative despite the monthly PAYEMS increase ≥50,000, or the effect is not statistically significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1350 units in the next 2 months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as strong consumer demand boosts corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the 2-month HOUST level exceeding 1350, or the effect is not robust across multiple out-of-sample windows.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 5 points predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as weak manufacturing signals near-term pessimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by ≥5 points in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day (or 5-day) forward returns are positive despite the monthly INDPRO decline, or the effect is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and improved investor sentiment.
failure_condition: Forward returns remain negative despite the two-month UNRATE decline below 4.0%, or the effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 2% and 5% respectively over the next quarter suggest dual demand drivers, predicting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↑ ≥2% AND RSAFS ↑ ≥5% in the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p>0.05), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 305 for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as lower inflation reduces discounting of future earnings.
failure_condition: Forward returns are negative despite the three-month CPIAUCSL decline below 305, or the effect is not robust across multiple inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: If INDPRO and GDPC1 both show a double-dip decline (each down at least 7 points in the next month), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to persistent supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO ↓ ≥7 AND GDPC1 ↓ ≥7 in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the double dip in both series, or the interaction effect is not significant.
